messages:
maria: Heads-up — I pushed a Grafana prototype for prompt cache hit trends: per-model / per-route / per-customer token-saved and hit-rate panels. Link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/prompt-cache-hittrend :eyes:

chris: Nice. Is that showing absolute tokens saved or normalized by requests?

maria: Both. Top row is raw tokens_saved, bottom row is tokens_saved_per_1k_requests. Also included a heatmap of hit-rate by hour for quick anomaly spotting.

lee: Can we slice by customer on the heatmap? Last week AcmeCorp had weird regressions we never traced.

maria: Yup — there's a customer dropdown. I preloaded a 7d window default. For AcmeCorp I see a 12% drop in hit-rate on redwood-v1-small around Wed 02:00 UTC. Tokens_saved also down ~18%.

aj: Any known rollout or kernel change around that time? batching heuristics maybe?

maria: We had a minor key-normalization change in runtime on Tue night (PR #4823) — it removed a trailing-space normalization for legacy prompts to reduce canonicalization costs. That increased key variance for templates that end with a newline.

chris: Interesting — so cache key cardinality went up and hit-rate fell. Do we have a quick query to quantify new key-per-req ratio?

maria: I added a sampling job in analytics that logs sampled prefix_hash per request. Quick SQL (in the dashboard query editor):

```sql
SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) AS hour,
       model,
       route,
       customer,
       COUNT(DISTINCT prefix_hash) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0) AS unique_prefix_per_req
FROM sampled_prefix_hashes
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
ORDER BY 1;
```

maria: For AcmeCorp + redwood-v1-small that metric jumps from 0.11 -> 0.32 at the regression time.

aj: Ouch. That aligns. We should either revert the normalization change or add a lightweight normalization for only common templates. Could we do a fallback that normalizes only when cache hit-rate dips?

lee: Also worth looking at batching interplay — if batcher groups by route/model and now keys are more varied, we might see smaller effective batch sizes which hurts latency and cost. The dashboard has a panel for avg_batch_size too.

chris: For alerts, can we set an automated rule like: when model-level hit-rate drops >5% AND tokens_saved delta < -10% for 3 consecutive hours, create a SEV2 and tag infra + runtime?

maria: Done in the prototype: alert rule name "prompt_cache_regression" — triggers on metric `prometheus.prompt_cache_hit_rate` with a customer dimension. I kept cooldown 3h to avoid flapping.

analytics-bot: [analytics] generated report: AcmeCorp — redwood-v1-small: 2026-03-10 01:40 UTC — hit_rate delta -12.3%, tokens_saved -17.6%, estimated cost increase $1.2k/week at current traffic. Report ID: r-20260310-17

chris: Good to have the cost estimate. For mitigation: short-term revert + rollout rollback. Medium-term: add a routing policy that falls back to a quantized key schema for high-cardinality customers.

maria: Proposal in the dashboard notes: add a "light-normalize" transform (strip trailing whitespace + collapse multiple newlines) applied selectively by customer/route via a config map. I can prototype and A/B against current using the rollout system.

aj: One more ask — add a panel that shows the ratio of 'warmup_hits' (hits served by prefetch/warmup) vs on-demand hits. That'll tell us whether our warmup prefetches are effective per customer.

maria: Will add it. Query will use `prefix_cache_hit_type` label (values: on_demand, warmup).

lee: Great. Once changes are validated, add a dashboard widget with a one-click rollback link to the deployment that touched key-normalization. Helps SREs respond faster.

maria: Agreed. I'll push the dashboard updates and attach runbook steps in the panel description. If anyone wants edit access ping me. :thumbsup:
